answerNotes.JOHN: Bible baptizer at the Jordan River. This scene follows Matthew 3:13–17; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.RIVER: A river is flowing water in a channel. In the baptism scene, Jordan is the proper name of the river.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.VOICE: A voice is the sound produced when someone speaks or sings. A speaker is the device that reproduces the sound on a call or recording.
answerNotes.SON: Son names a male child in a family. The same word applies to the relationship when the child has grown into an adult.
answerNotes.JORDAN: River where John baptized Jesus. This scene follows Matthew 3:13–17; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.FISH: Fish live in water and breathe through gills. A seal or otter swims too, but it is a mammal rather than a fish.
answerNotes.JOHN: The New Testament includes both John the Baptist and John the fisherman. The Jordan baptism scene uses the former; the fishing scene uses the latter.
answerNotes.SHORE: Shore is land at the edge of water. It can border a lake as well as the sea.
answerNotes.CALL: Call can mean telephone contact or saying a name aloud. Both uses involve trying to get someone's attention.
answerNotes.NET: Mesh used by the fishermen to catch their food. This scene follows Matthew 4:18–22; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.FOLLOW: Go behind someone along the same path. This scene follows Matthew 4:18–22; the passage gives the story's context.

answerNotes.WATER: Liquid needed by plants. This scene follows John 2:1–11; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.WEDDING: Ceremony in which two people marry. This scene follows John 2:1–11; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.JAR: A jar has a wide opening that makes spooning and filling easier. A bottle usually has a narrower neck.
answerNotes.STONE: Stone is a piece of natural rock. A slab is a relatively flat piece, while gravel consists of many smaller pieces.
answerNotes.FEAST: A feast is a large celebratory meal. The meal's role depends on its story, such as welcoming a guest or celebrating a return.
answerNotes.MARY: Mary is named as Jesus' mother in the Gospels. A story's setting helps distinguish her from other women named Mary.

answerNotes.DOOR: A door is the movable panel at an entrance. Hinges let it swing, while a latch or lock holds it closed.

answerNotes.WIND: Wind has two pronunciations and meanings: moving air, or turning something around a center. A yarn ball or clock uses the turning action.
answerNotes.PEACE: Peace can describe calm instead of conflict or disturbance. In the storm story, the setting concerns wind and water becoming still.
answerNotes.VOICE: A voice is the sound produced when someone speaks or sings. A speaker is the device that reproduces the sound on a call or recording.
answerNotes.STORM: Weather with strong wind and rain. This scene follows Mark 4:35–41; the passage gives the story's context.
answerNotes.CALM: Free from wind or rough waves. This scene follows Mark 4:35–41; the passage gives the story's context.
